entries.name: widening-is-never-recognised
entries.claim: A candidate release that adds an option to an already-released enum field is PLANNED, as one widenEnumDomain element, rather than refused with COMPILER_STORAGE_RETYPE_UNSUPPORTED. This is the fence PUR-2c measured; a planner that never recognises the widening refuses every option-list change as a retype.

kills.name: an enum-domain widening plans exactly one widenEnumDomain element, and every adjacent option-list change stays refused

entries.name: widening-admits-any-option-change
entries.claim: Only a STRICT SUPERSET of the previous option ids is a widening. With the subset test removed, a narrowing (one option removed) is admitted as if it widened -- the first of the preserved refusals to fall.

kills.name: an enum-domain widening plans exactly one widenEnumDomain element, and every adjacent option-list change stays refused

entries.name: widening-ignores-everything-but-the-id-set
entries.claim: A widening is admitted only when the candidate field, with its NEW option records removed, fingerprints byte-for-byte as the previous release did -- so a changed label or orderKey on an EXISTING option, a reordering, or any other column property is refused alongside the widening. Round-1 finding: the round-1 predicate excluded the whole fingerprint and let widening-plus-relabel through. This mutation makes the fingerprint comparison vacuous; the first case it admits is widening plus a relabelled existing option.

kills.name: an enum-domain widening plans exactly one widenEnumDomain element, and every adjacent option-list change stays refused

entries.name: checks-are-matched-by-name-only
entries.claim: A released CHECK that matches the previous release BY NAME is compared by DEFINITION before it is skipped. Matching by name alone is PUR-2c's observed hole: the physical name derives from the field id, so a widened option list produced zero elements and the release activated against the stale constraint.

kills.name: an enum-domain widening plans exactly one widenEnumDomain element, and every adjacent option-list change stays refused
kills.expected: the widening plans one element and nothing else

entries.name: old-readers-are-told-widening-is-transparent
entries.claim: The compatibility cell states oldRead: requiresReadFallback -- a reader compiled against N options observes the (N+1)th the moment a new writer stores it, and the matrix says so rather than calling the widening transparent.

kills.name: an enum-domain widening plans exactly one widenEnumDomain element, and every adjacent option-list change stays refused
kills.expected: the widening plans one element and nothing else

entries.name: provider-never-executes-the-enum-widening
entries.claim: widenEnumDomainCheck really runs the single-statement DROP CONSTRAINT, ADD CONSTRAINT ... NOT VALID against PostgreSQL. The switch is not exhaustiveness-checked, so an element applied with no DDL leaves every other gate green; the catalog verification inside prepare is what observes the missing definition.

entries.name: replay-reissues-the-ddl
entries.claim: A prepare whose target option set is already within the live constraint applies the element with NO DDL, so a replay -- the same widened release prepared again, here by the second tenant -- leaves the constraint's OID untouched. Without the early return the constraint is dropped and re-added on every prepare.

entries.name: element-narrows-a-divergent-live-constraint
entries.claim: The element NEVER narrows. A target whose option set diverges from the live constraint -- neither a subset nor a superset -- is refused with ENUM_DOMAIN_NARROWING_REJECTED before any DDL. With the guard removed the live constraint is replaced by the divergent set, and the mixed-root catalog verification is what then refuses it, for a different reason.

entries.name: repair-before-measure
entries.claim: AGENTS.md section 6's subject-repaired-before-measured vector, and PUR-2c section 2.4b's assertion 9. The previous release's CHECK must REJECT the option it does not declare, as SQLSTATE 23514 from that constraint, BEFORE the widening is measured. A constraint that constrains nothing makes every post-transition acceptance vacuous, and the catalog verifier agrees with itself either way; only the pre-state rejection observes it. The tautology is `col = col` because PostgreSQL re-renders `IS NOT DISTINCT FROM` as `NOT ... IS DISTINCT FROM` and the catalog verifier would then drift at the first prepare, for a reason that is not this one.

entries.name: missing-check-is-repaired-not-refused
entries.claim: An ABSENT released enum-domain CHECK is refused as catalog drift (ENUM_DOMAIN_CHECK_MISSING), never added. Round-1 finding: adding the target constraint NOT VALID when the table admitted everything is a pre-approval TIGHTENING that can newly refuse an update to a drifted row, and it repairs the drift before catalog verification measures it. With the refusal replaced by the round-1 repair, the drifted tenant's prepare succeeds and the verifier never sees the missing constraint.
